rationale: Prashanth and colleagues reviewed 307 Wilson disease records. The original results list drooling among presenting features in eight cases. Two example cases document initial diagnoses and subsequent recognition of Wilson disease. The measured count describes Wilson disease presentation. The article provides no raw fig exposure, Parkinson drooling severity comparison, or dietary response. Original journal pages 907-909 were inspected through the public version-of-record reproduction.

Brown and colleagues report the crystallographic structure of bacterial flagellar rotor protein FliG. Orange appears in the structure and sequence illustrations. The original reports no orange fruit intervention, human Parkinson cohort, or clinical falls.

The genomic comparison analyzes conservation and evolution of human disease gene orthologs in rats and mice. Orange identifies plotted repeat-length comparisons. The original reports no raw orange exposure or fall-frequency comparison in Parkinson disease.

Platelet serotonin content, uptake and secretion were measured in Parkinson disease, essential tremor, essential tremor plus and healthy comparator groups. This is a biomarker study. No fresh sage exposure or measured dystonia response to that ingredient appears in the clinical comparison.

The report uses genetic testing and functional imaging to characterize a cognitive-predominant spinocerebellar ataxia type 8 presentation. The report provides no ground sage exposure or rigidity comparison in Parkinson disease.

MEDIOLA compares anticancer treatment cohorts in relapsed ovarian cancer. The adverse-event table includes headache and the analysis describes dates of progression. Calendar dates and treatment adverse events provide no dried-date or Parkinson pain comparison.

The Care4Youngdem article reports palliative care and advance care planning perspectives in young-onset dementia. The cohort table records dates of diagnosis. Clinical dates and caregiver narratives provide no dried-date intervention or Parkinson pain outcome.

A chronic lead toxicity case describes action-predominant jerky movement and ataxia. The discussion lists abdominal pain as a possible lead-toxicity presentation. The original provides no date-fruit exposure or Parkinson pain comparison.

The PREVENT-AD study protocol compares intergenerational physical activity programming in adults at risk of Alzheimer disease. The original specifies exercise, social and cognitive assessments. There is no separately assigned dried-date intervention and no results for a Parkinson pain comparison in this protocol.

Thirteen people with Parkinson disease completed airway-protection interviews and questionnaires. The interview material includes distinct reports of swallowing difficulty, throat clearing, perceived excess saliva and nighttime drooling. The study did not assign dried dates or estimate their effect on pain. Airway and drooling experience are useful context, with no ingredient-specific response.

The diffuse axonal injury cohort compares serial neuron-specific enolase and Glasgow Coma Scale measurements with later neurological function. A registry date is a calendar value. The analysis provides no dried-date intervention or Parkinson pain response.

The controlled first-in-human study tests synthetic plasmalogen precursor PPI-1011 for pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability. Fifty-six healthy participants enrolled. This is a synthetic lipid drug and vehicle comparison. No date-fruit treatment or pain outcome in Parkinson disease was assessed.

The dermatology case describes skin lesions and diagnosis of blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm. The opening uses date in reference to time of diagnosis. The original contains no dried-date or Parkinson pain exposure–outcome comparison.

The vascular case describes endovascular management of an ascending aortic pseudoaneurysm and pericardial drainage. The procedure and clinical timing provide no dried-date or Parkinson pain comparison.

The case reports postictal encephalopathy and tracks alertness and EEG after amantadine. Parkinson disease appears in the background description of the medication. The original provides no dried-date exposure or Parkinson pain comparison.

The prospective open-label INLEVO-LIFE PD study evaluates inhaled levodopa for OFF episodes and measures quality of life and nonmotor symptoms. Any symptom changes belong to a medication cohort. No isolated dried-date exposure or date-specific pain response was evaluated.

The investigators randomized 159 people with early to moderate Parkinson disease to meditation, yoga or control. Methods and outcome tables describe mental health, motor and inflammatory measures. Fig. labels identify study illustrations. No raw fig exposure or raw-fig rest tremor comparison was assessed.

The case describes rapidly progressive parkinsonism during Acanthamoeba encephalitis. The narrative includes upper-limb tremulousness and reports diagnostic evidence from tissue. The source concerns infectious secondary parkinsonism. Fig. is a figure marker. It provides no fig treatment or Parkinson rest tremor response.

The study compares three-dimensional gait measures by motor subtype in Parkinson disease. It uses resting tremor among clinical features and describes recorded falls and standard clinical scales. Motor subtype and gait comparisons provide no raw fig exposure or assigned rest tremor response. Fig. introduces illustrations.

The Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative cohort analysis associates a baseline FIB-4 estimate of liver fibrosis with motor ratings in 360 people with Parkinson disease. A fibrosis marker and a motor score do not provide a raw fig or ingredient-specific rest tremor comparison.

The study uses focused ultrasound thalamotomy as a timed setting for plasma biomarker measurements. It reports elevated GFAP at 48 hours and depicts individual biomarker trajectories. Figures show intervention and biomarker measurements. The original contains no raw fig exposure or dietary rest tremor response.

The Parkinson case describes a new ataxic syndrome with imaging evidence of superficial siderosis. Rest tremor appears in the explanation of Parkinson diagnostic criteria. Figures illustrate imaging. The manuscript provides no raw fig treatment or measured response of rest tremor to fig.

The population-based parkinsonism cohort estimates dementia cumulative incidence of 69.3% at 20 years across the cohort and 67.8% in the Parkinson disease group. The effect estimates concern dementia and clinical risk markers. Figure references do not establish common fig exposure or rest tremor response.

The investigators retrospectively analyze nonmotor symptoms among 232 patients at a movement disorders clinic. Outcomes are clinical scale scores rather than a food intervention. The original provides no consumed baked turkey comparison or attributable olfactory response. Geographic references do not establish an edible exposure.

The early-Parkinson imaging study contrasts resting functional connectivity in people with or without probable REM sleep behavior disorder and healthy controls. The clinical table reports MDS-UPDRS domains. Date of birth is a demographic field. No dried-date intervention or individually attributable apathy change is reported.

The Australian support-service chart study compares caregiver-rated neuropsychiatric symptoms and distress by recorded psychological trauma history. Individual NPI domains appear in an adjusted logistic model. The exposure is prior psychological trauma. Reported neuropsychiatric symptoms contribute no dried-date direction for Parkinson apathy.

The study relates resting-state connectivity to cognition and depressive symptoms in older adults across two datasets. Apathy is named among potentially related factors in the limitations. The original provides no dietary dried-date contrast or independent Parkinson apathy treatment result.

The Parkinson biomarker study evaluates ZNF746 genetic variants and plasma Parkin, PINK1 and ZNF746. Database access dates appear in the methods. The measured exposures are genetic and laboratory variables. No dried-date apathy comparison is reported.

The case describes severe apathy and behavior change during cognitive decline. Neuropathological examination identified multiple degenerative processes. An individual symptom history without date-fruit exposure or a comparison supplies clinical context only.

The Fox Insight observational analysis compares self-reported physical activity with patient-reported cognitive problems. It identifies apathy among factors that it could not control for. The original has no dried-date intervention and no separate apathy effect estimate for a dietary exposure.

A randomized pilot compares remotely delivered meditation and breathwork with a waitlist in Parkinson disease. The paper provides an anxiety outcome table and discusses feasibility and baseline imbalance. The intervention is behavioral. It does not provide ground sage exposure or an isolatable sage effect on fall frequency.

The digital health survey includes 492 people with Parkinson disease and 75 with immune-mediated inflammatory disease. It evaluates willingness and barriers to capturing everyday health data. A patient survey on monitoring provides no fresh sage exposure or measured fatigue response attributable to sage.

The observational cohort characterizes juvenile parkinsonism in MCT8 deficiency and response to levodopa/carbidopa. Orange on a figure marks participants with gastric feeding tubes. The clinical exposure is medication and the orange mark is a figure color. No raw orange intervention or fall-frequency response is reported.

The imaging and clinical modeling study classifies Parkinson disease, multiple system atrophy and progressive supranuclear palsy. Some plots use orange to distinguish labeled groups. The original does not assign raw orange or quantify a dietary fall-frequency response.
